title: Accretion needs a named face
claim: Accretion laws over abstract names (a board grown from a seed, each step decided by the radius-r view of a site, values from a finite alphabet, every fair order counted). (G1) If no action closes a cycle, each component of every limit is the seed's with trees attached, of asymptotic dimension at most 1; since closing a cycle is naming a face, this follows from the frozen definition. (G2) A radius-2 law with coordinates mod 3 and an arrow that closes squares grows the square spiral, the plane, in its only order. (G2') The arrow is not needed: with coordinates mod 3 alone, a site enabled when its radius-2 view is one of the spiral head's 77 views grows the same spiral (Lemma S: the views repeat every three rings, so a check to ring 40 covers them). (G3) For every radius r >= 2 and every fixed priority of the four offsets, the square-closing law SQ_r has a fair order whose limit is not the square grid; for r <= 1 it closes no square. With the same nine values a static law that names the square allows the plane's cylinders and tori (BARE-NAMES-20261110-001A, T4). Revised after an independent review before publication.
failure_conditions: An accretion law that closes no cycle with a limit component other than a seed component with trees attached (against G1).
A fair order of the spiral law whose limit is not the square grid, or a turn at which its board is not the expected block (against G2).
A step of the arrow-free spiral at which a place other than the head has one of the head's views, or a view not covered by the check (against G2').
A radius r >= 2 and a priority for which every fair order of the square-closing law has the square grid as its limit (against G3).
foundation_claim_scope: Accretion laws over a countably infinite set of names with no letters; growth from a seed, every fair order; the plane as the square grid. Growth order is not part of the world (GROWTH-LAW-20261107-001).

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the coordinator's go-ahead on 2026-11-10; read twice before publication by an independent referee (a fresh Claude agent given the proof). Its arrow-free spiral became G2', its fixes to G1 and G3 were made, and its second pass found G2' with Lemma S and the priority form of G3 sound; both were checked independently in check.py.
validation.status: proved by hand; finite checks in check.py passed (result.json): P1 to P3 as frozen, P4 and P5 added after the review; read twice by an independent referee, sound after fixes
validation.novelty: Elementary; the spiral and the order-splitting argument are standard ideas in growth processes; folklore risk high. The arrow-free spiral is the referee's construction, proved here.
